relevance_note: Single case report of a girl with Blau syndrome carrying a NOD2 variant: "Genetic testing identified a heterozygous pathogenic NOD2 mutation, c.1558C>T (p.H520Y)".
method_note: Read the paper by hand; no table transcription. One first-hand patient (label 'patient', rule 5). Two previously published children from the Discussion are included under the v4 passing-mention rule because individual-level features are given: 'ref [7] patient' (Kurokawa et al.; iris bombe, secondary angle-closure glaucoma, posterior synechiae) and 'ref [8] patient' (Magliyah et al.; bilateral panuveitis). The ref [7] child is not explicitly called Blau syndrome in its own sentence (only by the surrounding context about intraocular surgery in Blau syndrome), so its disease label is 'not reported'. Kreps et al. [3] (8 patients) is group-level only and gets no rows. Age at onset and age at diagnosis for the patient are given only relative to presentation ('about 4 years earlier'; diagnosed 'May 2022, approximately 3 years and 3 months before presentation'), so both ages are 'not reported'; the stated age 7-year-4-month-old is age at presentation (August 2025), recorded as age at last evaluation although the final exam was about 3 months later. Joint swelling of ankles, hand interphalangeal joints and knees was recorded as arthritis observed; flexion deformities of the PIP joints as camptodactyly observed. Temporal change, not contradiction: IOP was normal at presentation (excluded row) but secondary glaucoma with IOP 26.7 mmHg developed in the right eye postoperatively; the checklist glaucoma item is observed. Similarly anterior chamber inflammation absent at presentation and keratic precipitates/cells absent at the final exam are excluded rows tied to those timepoints, while uveitic changes and keratic precipitates were observed earlier. OCT 'findings suggestive of retinal edema' is hedged and was not recorded. No skin, fever or inflammatory-marker data for the patient. Variant type not stated by authors; inheritance and parental testing not reported. Vital status not stated.

treatment_summary.value: methotrexate, diclofenac and adalimumab; oral prednisone 5 mg daily; sequential bilateral manual small-incision cataract surgery with posterior synechiolysis, in-the-bag IOL implantation, posterior capsulotomy and anterior vitrectomy; postoperative IV dexamethasone and topical drops; adalimumab replaced by tofacitinib with intensified therapy (prednisone 15 mg, methotrexate, naproxen); peripheral iridectomy and membrane removal in the right eye
span: She was treated with methotrexate, diclofenac, and adalimumab, with good control of articular manifestations.
maintained on oral prednisone 5 mg daily, oral methotrexate 10 mg once weekly, and subcutaneous adalimumab 20 mg every 3 weeks
In both eyes, manual small-incision cataract surgery was performed with posterior synechiolysis, in-the-bag intraocular lens (IOL) implantation, 23-G posterior capsulotomy, and anterior vitrectomy.

adalimumab was discontinued and replaced by tofacitinib. The intensified treatment included topical tobramycin–dexamethasone ointment, fluorometholone eye drops, pranoprofen eye drops, compound tropicamide eye drops, oral prednisone 15 mg daily, tofacitinib 7.5 mg daily, methotrexate 7.5 mg weekly, and naproxen 0.1 g daily.
Peripheral iridectomy and removal of the visible fibrocellular inflammatory membrane were performed in the right eye
